text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 0.78% today, extending a strong two-week rally of 8.1%, as oil refining fundamentals tightened further. U.S. crude prices held steady above $107 per barrel while refineries ran at 96.8% capacity—near maximum utilization—and diesel inventories fell to historically low levels at 107.9 million barrels. This combination of high refinery utilization and tight product supply typically widens the margin refiners earn on each barrel processed, which directly boosts profitability for companies like Marathon.

The broader backdrop of geopolitical risk and supply concerns also supports the energy sector. News of drone strikes targeting Mecca, competing claims over the Suez and Hormuz shipping corridors, and moves by major oil producers to develop new regions all underscore persistent tension over global oil supplies. Even as Saudi Arabia announced a damaged pipeline would restart soon—which briefly weighed on crude prices today—the underlying reality of stretched refinery capacity and historically tight diesel markets keeps the environment favorable for refiners.
